title: Customer support queries and mutations allow unauthenticated cross-tenant access
description: In the pre-patch release candidate, getCustomerTickets, getCustomerTicketThread and addCustomerReply trusted caller-supplied businessId and requesterEmail without validating an active authenticated session.
root_cause: app/convex/support.ts relied on client-supplied parameters for ticket querying and creation instead of deriving tenant identity from a server-verified session.
intended_behavior: Only authenticated merchants with verified session tokens can access tickets and replies belonging to their business.

trace.description: Caller invokes getCustomerTickets with an unverified businessId or email
Tickets table is queried by businessId without ownership validation
Tickets belonging to arbitrary businesses are returned to the caller

evidence.description: Pre-patch getCustomerTickets lacked requireBusinessOwner or session validation checks

conditions.description: Caller can send queries directly to public Convex endpoint

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated remote user or untrusted client.
instructions: Invoke getCustomerTickets with a victim businessId
Observe full ticket list returned without authentication check
execution.observed_result: Support tickets of other tenants were exposed.

remediation.strategy: Introduced getVerifiedCustomerIdentity helper and supportSessions table in Convex; mandate verified session token on all customer ticket read/write operations.

code_changes.fixed_code: const identity = await getVerifiedCustomerIdentity(ctx, args.sessionToken, args.businessId);

likelihood.reason: The Convex query was exposed publicly and required only an identifier.

impact.reason: Direct exposure of confidential customer and merchant support correspondence.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in source analysis and verified by negative security test app/tests/security.test.ts.

title: Internal team ticket operations trust client-provided email string
description: In the pre-patch release candidate, requireTeamPermission accepted adminEmail from the caller and checked adminUsers by email without verifying an active session token.
root_cause: Client context passed adminEmail in team queries/mutations which backend accepted as truth.
intended_behavior: Operations and team handlers must authenticate callers via server-verified session tokens.

trace.description: Caller invokes getTeamTickets with adminEmail parameter
Helper looks up user by email string without checking session token
Privileged internal tickets and internal notes exposed to unauthenticated caller

evidence.description: Pre-patch requireTeamPermission did not validate session token

conditions.description: Convex client query invocation over public API

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker who knows or guesses a team member's email address.
instructions: Send Convex query getTeamTickets with adminEmail parameter set to admin@zackisch.com
Observe team tickets and confidential internal notes returned
execution.observed_result: Internal team ticket thread and staff notes returned without password or token proof.

remediation.strategy: Enforce sessionToken argument in requireTeamPermission and validate token against active session before granting access.

likelihood.reason: Admin email addresses are predictable or readily discoverable.

impact.reason: Access to all support tickets, merchant metadata, and private staff notes.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in source analysis and verified in app/tests/security.test.ts.

title: Financial statements and setup readiness exposed without ownership authorization
description: In the pre-patch release candidate, getSetupReadiness, getFeeStatements, and generateMonthlyFeeStatement accepted businessId without validating that the calling user owned or belonged to that business.
root_cause: Missing requireBusinessOwner calls in app/convex/setup.ts financial and readiness handlers.
intended_behavior: All financial, invoicing, and readiness operations must require authenticated merchant ownership.

trace.description: Caller requests fee statements for arbitrary businessId
Database queries feeStatements table by businessId with no auth check
Tax information, bank details, and monthly financial summaries returned

evidence.description: Pre-patch getFeeStatements had no caller identity verification

execution.attacker_perspective: An authenticated or unauthenticated user querying another merchant's financial records.
instructions: Call getFeeStatements with victim business ID
Observe complete monthly billing statements and tax breakdown returned
execution.observed_result: Financial statements returned for businesses not owned by the caller.

remediation.strategy: Call requireBusinessOwner in getSetupReadiness, getFeeStatements, and restrict generateMonthlyFeeStatement to internal callers.

likelihood.reason: Direct query callable with any known business ID.

impact.reason: Exposure of sensitive merchant financial data and revenue metrics.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in source analysis and verified in app/tests/security.test.ts.

title: Operations session credentials stored without cryptographic verification
description: Pre-patch admin context in internal app stored ops credentials in localStorage and relied on client-side state without enforcing server-validated session tokens on Convex queries.
root_cause: Trusting client-persisted role flags and raw email in localStorage.
intended_behavior: Operations session must validate cryptographic tokens on every server call.

trace.description: Client reads localStorage admin session data
Client passes email and role to application pages
Client executes operations based on untrusted localStorage flags

evidence.description: Admin context loaded unvalidated localStorage strings

conditions.description: Browser client running internal admin app

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker with physical or local script access to a browser, or tampering with localStorage.
instructions: Modify localStorage keys in internal app
execution.observed_result: Client-side elevation permitted access to admin screens.

remediation.strategy: Bind all operations to backend-verified session tokens and require sessionToken in all privileged Convex handlers.

likelihood.reason: Requires local browser manipulation or cross-site script injection.

impact.reason: Privilege escalation to internal admin tooling.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in code review and remediated in Phase A.

title: Cross-domain support handoff lacked durable server-side session binding
description: Handoff tokens between app.zackisch.com and support.zackisch.com were consumed into localStorage without creating a durable, server-verified support session, allowing ticket URL query parameter spoofing.
root_cause: app/convex/support.ts did not persist support sessions, and support ticket view trusted email query parameters in URLs.
intended_behavior: Support handoff must atomically exchange a one-time token for a server-managed support session with secure cookie or token transport.

trace.description: Page reads email query parameter from URL
Page passes URL email parameter to getCustomerTicketThread
Thread returned if email matches ticket requesterEmail, exposing ticket details

evidence.description: URL searchParams.get('email') used directly as authorization parameter

conditions.description: Ticket links shared or logged in browser history

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker who observes or guesses a ticket URL with an email parameter.
instructions: Open ticket URL with victim email in query string
execution.observed_result: Support ticket history and replies viewable without authentication.

remediation.strategy: Created supportSessions table in Convex schema; removed email query parameter; require verified session token stored on ticket exchange.

code_changes.fixed_code: supportSessions: defineTable({ sessionToken: v.string(), businessId: v.id('businesses'), requesterEmail: v.string(), expiresAt: v.number() })

likelihood.reason: URLs with email query parameters leak in browser history, logs, and referral headers.

impact.reason: Unauthorized access to customer support correspondence.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in source analysis and verified in app/tests/security.test.ts.

title: POS reconciliation status mutable without merchant staff authorization
description: In the pre-patch release candidate, recordOrderInPos and getPosReconciliationSummary allowed callers to mark orders as entered into POS or inspect POS ledger totals without verifying the caller was authorized staff for that business.
root_cause: Missing business membership check in app/convex/orders.ts POS reconciliation routines.
intended_behavior: Only authorized staff members of the specific business can record orders in POS and access reconciliation summaries.

trace.description: Caller invokes mutation with orderId and posReference
Order fetched without verifying caller belongs to order business
Order marked as posEntered: true, altering reconciliation ledger

evidence.description: Pre-patch recordOrderInPos lacked staff identity verification

execution.attacker_perspective: A guest or competitor invoking Convex mutations directly.
instructions: Call recordOrderInPos mutation with order ID
Observe order marked as recorded in POS, corrupting merchant bookkeeper records
execution.observed_result: Order POS reconciliation status altered without merchant authorization.

remediation.strategy: Verify caller staff session or business ownership before allowing recordOrderInPos or getPosReconciliationSummary.

code_changes.fixed_code: const order = await ctx.db.get(args.orderId); if (!order) throw new Error('Order not found');

likelihood.reason: Requires knowledge of active order IDs.

impact.reason: Tampering with financial bookkeeper ledger and POS fiscalization tracking.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in source analysis and verified in app/tests/security.test.ts.
